contact.body: The founder answers, usually the same day.

items.a: No. Synq is an app inside your Shopify admin. Your store, theme, checkout and payments stay in Shopify. Synq adds your cards, keeps their prices in step and gets them ready for the counter.

items.q: Where do the prices come from?
items.a: From TCGplayer's market price: a rolling average of recently completed sales for each card. Synq brings it in every day, converts it to your store's currency, and your price rules decide what you charge.

items.q: I'm not in the US. Will the prices suit my market?
items.a: Prices come from the US market on TCGplayer, converted to your store's currency every day. Where your local market prices a card differently, adjust the rule's margin for that game or set the card's price by hand.

Magic: The Gathering, Pokémon (English and Japanese), Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece, Lorcana, Riftbound, Digimon, Gundam, Union Arena, Weiss Schwarz, Star Wars Unlimited, Dragon Ball Super: Fusion World, Flesh and Blood, Sorcery, Grand Archive and more. If a game you sell is on TCGplayer but missing here, ask for it with "Request this game" in the spreadsheet import, or write to us.

Each condition is a variant on the card's Shopify product. When you add a card, you pick the condition it's in, and a played copy is one more add. Each condition can follow its own TCGplayer market price.

items.q: Can I set my own price on a card?
items.a: Yes. Set a card's price in Synq and price rules leave that condition alone from then on. A price changed in the Shopify admin is not protected: the next rule run sets it again, unless you exclude that condition. A rule can also have a minimum based on your cost, so a card is never priced below it.

items.q: Can I bring in the cards I already sell?
items.a: Yes. Export your inventory from TCGplayer, or save any spreadsheet as CSV, TSV or TXT, and import it. Synq matches each row to the catalog and creates what's new, without duplicates. For cards you already sell, you choose: add the file's stock, replace it, or leave them as they are (a TCGplayer export replaces by default). When a name fits several printings, you pick the one on your shelf.

items.q: Does Synq update my TCGplayer store?
items.a: No. TCGplayer doesn't open its API to apps like Synq, so it can't list cards or change stock there. Synq keeps your Shopify store in step, online and at the counter.

items.q: Can I sell at the counter?
items.a: Yes, with Shopify POS. Sealed products use the barcode printed on the box, and every single gets its own code for each condition. Print labels with Shopify's free Retail Barcode Labels app, and a scan rings up the exact card and condition, with stock updated online too.

items.q: What happens after the free trial?
items.a: Paid plans start with 7 days free. If you don't pick a plan, your account moves to the Free plan, up to 100 cards. Nothing is deleted and your Shopify store keeps running. Billing goes on your Shopify invoice, and you can cancel anytime.

meta.title: Install Synq · Synq help center
meta.description: Install Synq from the Shopify App Store. It opens inside your Shopify admin and changes nothing in your store until you add or link a product.

install.title: Install Synq
install.intro: Install Synq from the Shopify App Store. It opens inside your Shopify admin and changes nothing in your store until you add or link a product.

sections.title: Install from the Shopify App Store
steps: Open the [Synq page on the Shopify App Store](https://apps.shopify.com/synq-tcg-card-manager).
Click install and pick the store you want to use.
Review the access Shopify shows and approve it.
Synq opens inside your Shopify admin on **Set up synq**.

sections.title: What Synq can see and change
paragraphs: Shopify asks you to approve this access when you install.
list: **Products:** products, variants, prices, images, SKUs, barcodes, collections and Cost per item.
**Stock:** quantities at each of your locations.
**Sales channels:** which channels a product is published to.
**Theme:** your theme's product templates, read only.

note.title: No orders or customers
note.body: Synq has no access to your orders, customers or payments. It stores no customer details.

sections.title: What you see first
paragraphs: Synq starts on **Set up synq** and stays there until you pick at least one game you sell.
After that, the left menu shows **Home**, **Add products**, **Inventory**, **Price rules** and **Settings**.
Nothing is copied from your store when you install. Products you already sell stay as they are until you link them.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Your products are safe.** Installing doesn't create, edit or delete anything in Shopify.
**Next step:** [The setup](/docs/setup) takes a couple of minutes and makes your first price rule.

meta.title: The setup: your games and first price rule · Synq help center
meta.description: The setup asks which games you sell, how you want to price, and where your cards are today. It saves your first price rule for you.

setup.title: The setup: your games and first price rule
setup.intro: The setup asks which games you sell, how you want to price, and where your cards are today. It saves your first price rule for you.

sections.title: The setup, step by step
paragraphs: The page is called **Set up synq** and shows "Step N of M" at the top. Press Enter or click **Continue** to move on.
Some stores see a shorter setup without the price and publishing steps. In that case your first rule starts at the market price, and you can change it later in **Price rules**.
steps: **Which games do you sell?** Tick every game you sell. Games your store already sells are ticked for you. You need at least one.
**Set your prices.** Pick your price compared with the TCGplayer market price, from 10% under to 10% over. Then pick how each condition is priced.
**What happens when you add a card?** Pick **Save it as a draft** or **Put it on sale right away**, and tick the sales channels under **Sell it on**.
**Where are your cards today?** Pick **Link my products**, **Import my file** or **Add my first cards**.
**You're set up.** Check the summary. Click **Change** on any row to go back to it.

sections.title: The price step
paragraphs: **Your price** sets where you sit against the TCGplayer market price: -10%, -5%, **Market**, +5% or +10%.
**Each condition** decides how played cards are priced:
list: **Its own TCGplayer price:** each condition follows its own market price. This is the default.
**Standard:** LP 10% off Near Mint, MP 25% off, HP 40% off, DMG 60% off.
**A little less:** LP 5% off, MP 15% off, HP 25% off, DMG 40% off.
**Same as Near Mint:** every condition at the Near Mint price.

sections.title: Minimum and rounding
paragraphs: Open **Minimum and rounding** under the price step to set two more things.
A sample card shows the market price and your price for each condition, so you can see the effect before you continue.
list: **Never below:** no minimum, or about $0.25, $0.50 or $1, converted to your store's currency.
**Rounding:** Exact, Up to .99, Up to .49 or Nearest whole.

sections.title: What the setup saves
list: **Your games.** Search in **Add products** shows these first.
**Draft or on sale,** and the sales channels new products go to.
**A price rule called "All products".** It covers every game, prices new products as you add them, and re-prices your inventory every day at 6:00 AM in your store's time zone.

note.title: Only one first rule
note.body: The setup makes the "All products" rule only when your store has no price rules yet.

sections.title: After the setup: Home
paragraphs: **Home** shows a guide called **Get your store ready**, one step at a time. You can hide it, and it goes away when the required steps are done.
steps: **Add your first 10 cards.** Search right in the step, or click **Add cards**.
**See a card on your store** (optional). **Change how cards read** opens **Settings** › **Online Store**.
**Put your cards in collections.** **Pick collections** opens **Settings** › **What you sell**.
**Check your first price update.** **See price updates** opens **Price rules**. This step is done after your first rule run.
**Sell in your physical store with Shopify POS** (optional). Shown only when Shopify POS is installed.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Drafts are the default.** Nobody sees a draft until you publish it in Shopify.
**Everything can change later.** Games are in **Settings** › **What you sell**. Prices are in **Price rules**.
**Your first price update** happens at the next 6:00 AM, or right away if you run the rule yourself. See [Preview, run and schedule](/docs/run-and-schedule).

Tick each game you sell. At least one game stays ticked.
Pick a **Singles collection** and a **Sealed collection** for each game, or **No collection**.
paragraphs: In **Add products**, the gear icon next to the game icons opens the same page.

sections.title: How collections work
paragraphs: A new single goes into its game's singles collection. A new sealed product goes into the sealed collection.
Home's step **Put your cards in collections** is done when every game you sell has a collection.
To add existing products to a collection, use **Inventory** › select products › ⋯ › **Add to collection(s)**.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Turning on a game imports nothing.** It only lets you add cards from it.
**Games don't have their own condition settings.** Conditions are the same for every game. See [Conditions and printings](/docs/conditions-printings).
**A game is missing.** Ask for it with **Request this game** in the spreadsheet import, or with **Feedback** on Home.

meta.title: Add cards and sealed · Synq help center
meta.description: Search a card or sealed product in Add products, pick the printing and condition, and Synq creates the Shopify product with its price.

add-cards.title: Add cards and sealed
add-cards.intro: Search a card or sealed product in **Add products**, pick the printing and condition, and Synq creates the Shopify product with its price.

sections.title: Search
paragraphs: Results show as you type. A search needs at least 2 characters.
Search by card name or number. The icons above the results narrow it to one game, or **All**.
With an empty search, the page shows **Sets you added from recently** and **Recently added**.

sections.title: Search inside a set with @
list: **@ alone** lists the latest sets.
**@ plus a code or name,** like `@paf` or `@paldean fates`, suggests sets. Enter or Tab picks the first one.
**A picked set** shows as a chip. With an empty search you see the whole set in order.
**To remove a set,** click × on the chip or press Backspace.

sections.title: Read the results
paragraphs: Cards already in your store come first, under **In your store**. Everything else is under **More results**, 50 per page.
Each card has one row per printing, with its market price in your currency and your stock.
Click a printing's row to add it.

sections.title: Add a card
steps: Pick the **condition**. Each condition button shows its price. Sealed products are always Unopened.
Pick the **printing** and the **location**, if the card or your store has more than one.
Set the **quantity**.
Check the price. The chip next to it says which rule or exception sets it.
Check the status in the footer: **Creating as Draft** or **Active**. Click it to switch.
Click **Add to store**, or press Enter.
paragraphs: You add one condition at a time. To stock a Near Mint and a Lightly Played copy, add the card twice.

sections.title: Add more of a card you already have
paragraphs: When the printing is already in your store, the quantity is added to that condition at that location. You see "Stock updated".
A condition you didn't have yet becomes a new variant on the same product.
Adding stock keeps the card's current price. The next run of its rule updates it.

sections.title: More options before you add
list: **Pricing configuration:** see the rule that prices the card, set an exception, and enter what you paid. See [Exceptions](/docs/exceptions) and [Cost and margin](/docs/cost-margin).
**Title and collection** for a new product, plus its search engine title and description.
**Point of Sale:** the SKU and barcode, shown when Shopify POS is installed.
**Photo:** the printing's photo or the card image.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **No market price.** If TCGplayer has no price for that condition, type **Your price** to add it.
**Your own photos** can't be uploaded from Synq. Add them to the product in Shopify.
**Plan limit.** At your plan's product limit the add is refused. See [Plans and product limits](/docs/plans).
**Many cards at once.** Use [Import a spreadsheet](/docs/import).

meta.title: Conditions and printings · Synq help center
meta.description: Each printing of a card is its own Shopify product. Each condition is a variant of that product, with its own price and stock.

conditions-printings.title: Conditions and printings
conditions-printings.intro: Each printing of a card is its own Shopify product. Each condition is a variant of that product, with its own price and stock.

sections.title: How a card becomes a product
list: **One product per card and printing.** A Normal and a Foil copy of the same card are two products.
**One variant per condition.** The variants sit under one option called "Condition".
**Stock per condition and location.** Each variant tracks its own quantity.

sections.title: Conditions
paragraphs: Sealed products have one condition, Unopened.
Conditions are the same for every game.

sections.title: How condition names show in your store
steps: Open **Settings** › **Online Store** › **Condition variants**.
Under **Condition names**, pick full names (Near Mint) or abbreviations (NM).

note.title: New products only
note.body: The choice applies to products you add from then on. Products you already have keep their variant names.

sections.title: Printings
paragraphs: Printings come from TCGplayer: Normal, Foil, Holofoil, 1st Edition, Reverse Holofoil and more.
Each printing has its own market price, so a Foil is priced on its own.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Pokémon TCG Japan** is a separate game. Turn it on in **Settings** › **What you sell**.
**Removing a condition** deletes that variant in Shopify. Do it in **Inventory** with the **Conditions** panel.
**Played conditions with no market price** use the rule's percent below Near Mint. See [Build a price rule](/docs/price-rules).

meta.title: Link products you already have · Synq help center
meta.description: Link a product that's already in your Shopify store to its card. Synq keeps the product and takes over its price and stock.

link-products.title: Link products you already have
link-products.intro: Link a product that's already in your Shopify store to its card. Synq keeps the product and takes over its price and stock.

sections.title: Where to start
paragraphs: In **Add products**, open **Import** › **Link from Shopify**. In the setup, pick **Link my products**.

sections.title: Link a product
steps: **Link from Shopify** lists your store's products that aren't linked yet, newest first. Search with **Search your store's products**, then click one.
**Which card is it?** The search is filled with the product's title. Pick the card.
**Add to synq.** Pick the printing, then give each variant its condition.
Click **Add to synq**.

sections.title: What Synq fills in for you
list: **SKU of 1 to 9 digits:** read as a TCGplayer SKU, so the card is found for you.
**Barcode or SKU of 10 to 14 digits:** read as the product's UPC or EAN.
**Conditions:** read from the SKU or the variant's name. Words like "NM-M", "Light Play" and "Excellent" are understood.
**A card from a game you don't sell:** Synq offers **Enable** for that game.

sections.title: What happens after you link
list: **Nothing changes in Shopify at the moment you link.** Title and description stay as they are.
**Cost** is read from Shopify's Cost per item.
**Price** follows the product's price rule from the rule's next run.
**Stock** stays in sync from then on.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **One product at a time.** There is no bulk link yet.
**Check the rule first.** Open the rule's preview in **Price rules** to see the new price before it runs.
**All linked.** When every product is linked, the list says "Everything is in synq".

meta.title: Import a spreadsheet · Synq help center
meta.description: Import a CSV from TCGplayer or your own sheet. Synq matches every row to its card, creates what's new and adds stock to what you have.

import.title: Import a spreadsheet
import.intro: Import a CSV from TCGplayer or your own sheet. Synq matches every row to its card, creates what's new and adds stock to what you have.

sections.title: Where to start
paragraphs: In **Add products**, open **Import** › **From TCGplayer** or **From a spreadsheet**. In the setup, pick **Import my file**.
The page is called **Import a spreadsheet** and has four steps: **Spreadsheet**, **Columns**, **Review** and **Import**.

sections.title: Your file
list: **CSV, TSV or TXT.** Excel and Numbers files are refused. In Excel, use File › Save As › CSV.
**Any separator.** Tabs, semicolons and commas are found for you, and so is the text encoding.
**Title rows** above the header are fine.
**Each row needs** a product name, a barcode or a TCGplayer ID.
**Download a template** gives you a CSV with the columns ready.

sections.title: Columns
paragraphs: Synq reads headers in English and Spanish. Check each one in the **Columns** step, or set it to **Don't import**.
Columns it understands: Product name, TCGplayer ID, TCGplayer SKU, Barcode, Game, Set, Card number, Printing, Condition, Quantity, Location, Price, Cost and Status.
When a column is missing, each row gets a quantity of 1, your first location, your default condition and the market price.

sections.title: TCGplayer exports
paragraphs: A TCGplayer inventory export is found for you. Its rows carry the exact SKU, so card, printing and condition are exact.
It usually skips straight to **Review**. By default, its stock replaces the stock you have.

sections.title: Review
paragraphs: Synq matches rows by TCGplayer SKU first, then TCGplayer ID, barcode, exact name and close name.
Tabs show **All**, **New**, **In your store** and **To answer**.
A row that fits several products shows "{n} products fit". Pick the one on your shelf. A row with no match can be searched or left out.

sections.title: Import options
list: **Products you already sell:** **Add the sheet's stock**, **Make the sheet's stock their stock** or **Leave them as they are**.
**Price of new products:** **Your price rules** (the default) or **The price in your sheet**.
**New products start as:** what your sheet says, Draft or Active.
**Channels** for new products.
**Save the barcodes from your sheet** on the products.

sections.title: Run the import
paragraphs: The import runs in the background, so you can leave the page.
When it's done, rows that were left out download as a CSV with the reason on each row. Past imports are under **Sheets you imported**.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **5,000 products per import.** Split a bigger file.
**Plan limit.** New products past your plan's limit aren't created. Stock for products you already have still goes in.
**A game isn't in Synq.** Use **Request this game** in the import.
**There is no export.** Synq doesn't download your stock as a file.

meta.title: How market prices work · Synq help center
meta.description: Every price in Synq starts from the TCGplayer market price for that card, printing and condition. Your price rules turn it into your price.

market-prices.title: How market prices work
market-prices.intro: Every price in Synq starts from the TCGplayer market price for that card, printing and condition. Your price rules turn it into your price.

sections.title: Where the price comes from
list: **TCGplayer market price,** in US dollars.
**Per condition.** Each condition has its own market price.
**Fallback.** If Near Mint or a sealed product has no price of its own, the printing's market price is used.
**Updated once a day.** That's how often the market moves on TCGplayer.
paragraphs: In **Inventory**, hover the **Market** price to see TCGplayer's Market, Low, Mid and High.

sections.title: When your prices change
paragraphs: Your prices change only when a price rule runs. Between runs, nothing changes them.
The "All products" rule from the setup runs every day at 6:00 AM in your store's time zone.
You can also run any rule yourself. See [Preview, run and schedule](/docs/run-and-schedule).

sections.title: Your store's currency
list: **Followed for you.** Synq uses your Shopify store's currency. There is nothing to pick.
**Converted from US dollars** with current exchange rates.
**Minimum and rounding** work in your currency, after the conversion.

note.title: Unsupported currency
note.body: If Synq has no exchange rate for your currency, it can't price your cards. **Settings** shows "Unsupported currency". Tell us with **Feedback** on Home.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Prices are US market prices.** Where your local market differs, adjust the rule's percent for that game. See [Build a price rule](/docs/price-rules).
**No market price.** The rule preview lists these under **No market**. Set their price yourself with an [exception](/docs/exceptions).
**Synq doesn't update TCGplayer.** It only uses its prices.

meta.title: Build a price rule · Synq help center
meta.description: A price rule says which products it prices and how. Build one for every game, or one for a single game, set, rarity, printing or condition.

price-rules.title: Build a price rule
price-rules.intro: A price rule says which products it prices and how. Build one for every game, or one for a single game, set, rarity, printing or condition.

sections.title: Start a rule
steps: Open **Price rules**.
Click **New rule** and pick **Every game** or one of your games.
Name the rule (up to 40 characters).
Go through the four steps: **Define products**, **Define pricing**, **Define minimum** and **Confirm**.
paragraphs: A store can have up to 50 rules.

sections.title: Define products
list: **Sets** and **Rarities:** only in a rule for one game.
**Printings** and **Conditions:** NM to DMG, and Unopened for sealed.
**Applies to:** **New products** prices cards as you add or import them. **Your inventory** prices your stock each time the rule runs. Both are ticked at first.
paragraphs: Leave a limit empty to include everything. A rule for new products only has no schedule and no **Run**.

sections.title: Define pricing
list: **Base prices on:** the TCGplayer market price.
**Modify by:** a percent up or down, from -99% to +1000%.
**Then add:** an amount in your currency, up or down.

sections.title: Price each condition
paragraphs: Pick how played conditions are priced:
list: **Each condition's market price:** each condition follows its own TCGplayer price. This is the default.
**Near Mint's, less a percent:** every condition starts from Near Mint's price, less its percent.

sections.title: Below Near Mint
paragraphs: With **Each condition's market price**, these percents are used only for a played condition that has no market price of its own.
Leave a percent empty and that condition isn't priced. It keeps the price it has.

sections.title: Rounding, minimum and confirm
paragraphs: Pick a rounding in the pricing step, then a minimum. See [Minimums and rounding](/docs/minimums-rounding).
**Confirm** shows the whole rule. Click **Edit** on any part to change it.
When you save, the rule opens on its preview.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Saving doesn't change prices.** Prices change when the rule runs.
**One rule per condition.** When rules overlap, the most specific one prices the card. See [Which rule prices a product](/docs/which-rule-wins).
**A single card** can follow its own price. See [Exceptions](/docs/exceptions).

meta.title: Preview, run and schedule a rule · Synq help center
meta.description: Preview shows every price a rule would change. Run it yourself, or give it a schedule, and check what changed in Activity.

run-and-schedule.title: Preview, run and schedule a rule
run-and-schedule.intro: Preview shows every price a rule would change. Run it yourself, or give it a schedule, and check what changed in Activity.

sections.title: Preview a rule
paragraphs: Open a rule's ⋯ menu and click **Preview rule**. A saved rule also opens here.
Each product and condition shows its **Original price** and **Updated price**.
Tabs show **All**, **Go up**, **Go down**, **Unchanged**, **No market** and **Exceptions**. Search by name, set or condition, or filter by set.

sections.title: Run a rule
steps: In **Price rules**, click **Run** on the rule. In the preview, click **Run rule · N prices**.
Read the confirmation and click **Run**. Click **Preview first** to check the prices again.
The run is queued, then the prices change in Shopify.

note.title: A run can't be stopped
note.body: Once a run starts, it finishes. A run that's still queued can be cancelled.

sections.title: Schedule a rule
steps: Open the rule's ⋯ menu and click **Edit schedule** or **Add schedule**.
Pick **Every day**, **Some days** or **Once**. **Once** suits a sale: the rule runs that day and its schedule ends.
Pick the time, in 15-minute steps, in your store's time zone.
Set the status to **Active** or **Paused**.
paragraphs: Pause or resume from the ⋯ menu. **Remove schedule** turns the rule into one you run by hand.
Tabs on **Price rules** show **All**, **Scheduled**, **Paused** and **By hand**.

sections.title: Activity
paragraphs: **Activity**, next to your rules, lists every run with its time and how many prices went up or down.
Each run is **Queued**, **Running**, **Complete**, **Failed** or **Cancelled**. A calendar icon means it ran on its schedule.
Click a complete run to see every price it changed. Click **Retry** on a failed run.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Before your first run,** a banner offers to preview the rule first.
**One run at a time.** Runs in a store wait their turn.
**Missed times run late.** If Synq misses a scheduled time, the run happens late instead of being skipped, up to a day later.
**History.** Run details stay for 90 days and the list of runs for a year.

meta.title: Minimums and rounding · Synq help center
meta.description: A minimum keeps a card from selling under a price you pick. Rounding gives your prices clean endings.

minimums-rounding.title: Minimums and rounding
minimums-rounding.intro: A minimum keeps a card from selling under a price you pick. Rounding gives your prices clean endings.

sections.title: Set a minimum
paragraphs: In the rule's **Define minimum** step, pick one:
list: **None:** no minimum.
**A fixed amount:** in your store's currency.
**Your cost:** what you paid, plus or minus a percent or an amount. Never sold under what you paid.

sections.title: The same for every condition, or per condition
paragraphs: Pick **Same for every condition**, or **Per condition** to set one minimum for each.
Leave a condition empty and it has no minimum.

sections.title: Rounding
paragraphs: Pick rounding in the rule's **Define pricing** step:
list: No rounding
Round up to x.49
Round up to x.99
Round up to x.00
Round to nearest x.00

sections.title: Good to know
list: **No maximum.** Rules have a minimum but no ceiling.
**No cost, no cost minimum.** A product without a cost has no minimum based on cost, and the preview says so. See [Cost and margin](/docs/cost-margin).
**Your currency.** Minimum and rounding work after the conversion from US dollars.
**A card's own minimum.** When a product has its own minimum, the higher of the two wins. See [Exceptions](/docs/exceptions).
**Zero is never published.** A price of 0 or less is never sent to Shopify.

meta.title: Exceptions: set a card's price yourself · Synq help center
meta.description: An exception is a price setting a product has for itself. It wins over the rule that prices it.

exceptions.title: Exceptions: set a card's price yourself
exceptions.intro: An exception is a price setting a product has for itself. It wins over the rule that prices it.

sections.title: Three kinds of exception
list: **Own formula:** Market price, Market + % or Market - %, used instead of the rule's formula.
**Own minimum:** the higher of the product's minimum and the rule's minimum wins.
**Excluded from rules:** for one condition. No run changes its price. It shows as "Excluded from rules · not changed".

sections.title: Set your own price on a card
steps: Open **Inventory** and expand the product.
Edit the **Listed** price on the condition's row.
Save. That condition is now excluded from rules.
paragraphs: To hand the price back to its rule, click **Back to its rule** on that row.

sections.title: Other places to set an exception
list: **Inventory** › the product's **Exceptions** cell.
**Inventory** › select products › **Exceptions** panel, for many products at once.
**Add products** › **Pricing configuration** › **Exception**, when you add the card. Pick **Your price** to keep rules away from it.

sections.title: Find your exceptions
paragraphs: In **Inventory**, open **Views** and pick **Own formula** or **Excluded from rules**.
On **Price rules**, the line at the top counts your exceptions.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Prices edited in Shopify admin are overwritten** at the next run of the product's rule. Set the price in Synq instead, or exclude the condition.
**Excluded conditions keep their price for good,** even when the market moves. Check the **Excluded from rules** view now and then.

meta.title: Which rule prices a product · Synq help center
meta.description: Each condition of each product has one rule at most. When rules overlap, the most specific one prices it.

which-rule-wins.title: Which rule prices a product
which-rule-wins.intro: Each condition of each product has one rule at most. When rules overlap, the most specific one prices it.

sections.title: The most specific rule wins
paragraphs: Synq counts the limits a rule names: game, set, rarity, printing and condition. The rule that names the most limits and fits the product wins.
If two rules are equally specific, the newest one wins.

sections.title: An example
paragraphs: A Pokémon foil is priced by "Pokémon foils". A normal Pokémon card by "Pokémon". A Magic card by "All products".

sections.title: Products with no rule
paragraphs: A product that no rule covers is never touched by a run. It keeps its price.
A new product with no rule for **New products** gets the plain market price.
The line at the top of **Price rules** shows how many products are priced by a rule, how many have no rule, and how many have exceptions.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Exceptions win** over every rule. See [Exceptions](/docs/exceptions).
**Check before you run.** The preview shows which products a rule prices.
**Two rules never price the same condition** of the same product.

meta.title: Find and filter products · Synq help center
meta.description: Inventory lists every product Synq manages. Search, filter and save the views you use every day.

find-products.title: Find and filter products
find-products.intro: **Inventory** lists every product Synq manages. Search, filter and save the views you use every day.

sections.title: Open Inventory
paragraphs: Click **Inventory** in the left menu. Home and Add products call the same page **My products**.
Tabs show **All**, one tab per game, and **Views**.

sections.title: Search
paragraphs: **Search all products** looks in the card name, Shopify title, set name and code, number, printing, UPC, TCGplayer ID, SKU and barcode.
Every word has to match, so `Charizard PAF` narrows to one set.

sections.title: Filters and sort
list: **Vendor:** the game. Shown when you sell 2 or more games.
**Condition**
**Stock:** In stock or Sold out.
**Formula:** Follows its rule, Market price, Market + % or Market - %.
**Price rules:** Excluded from rules.
**Set name** and **Product type**
**Imported from:** shown after an import.
paragraphs: Sort by date created, product name, set name, price, cost or margin.

sections.title: Save a view
paragraphs: A view saves your filters, search and sort. Click **Save as view** and name it.
Change a view and click **Update** with its name to save it again. You can also rename or delete it.
Two views come ready: **Own formula** and **Excluded from rules**.

sections.title: Columns and rows
paragraphs: Pick columns with **Columns**: Printing, Rarity, Number, Stock, Exceptions, Market, Listed, Cost, Margin and Minimum. The choice is saved for your whole store.
Expand a product to see one line per condition and location, with its stock, market price, cost and **Listed** price.
Each row can **Set as active** or **Set as draft**, and open the card on TCGplayer or the product in Shopify.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **No filter for status, tags, collections or rarity.** Show the **Rarity** column and sort instead.
**Listed** is the price on Shopify. Editing it sets an exception. See [Exceptions](/docs/exceptions).

meta.title: Edit many products at once · Synq help center
meta.description: Select products in Inventory to change stock, cost, conditions or exceptions for all of them at once.

bulk-edit.title: Edit many products at once
bulk-edit.intro: Select products in **Inventory** to change stock, cost, conditions or exceptions for all of them at once.

sections.title: Select products
paragraphs: Tick the rows you want, or filter first and click **Select all N matching**.
A bar opens with four panels and a ⋯ menu.

sections.title: The four panels
list: **Stock:** add, remove or set a quantity for one condition at one location. Remove never goes below 0.
**Cost:** a share of the market price or an amount, for one condition or all. Tick **Replace costs already set** to overwrite. Prices don't change.
**Conditions:** remove conditions. This deletes those variants in Shopify.
**Exceptions:** set a formula, a minimum, excluded conditions or your price.

sections.title: The ⋯ menu
list: **Set as active** and **Set as draft**
**Add to collection(s)** and **Remove from collection(s):** manual collections only.
**Unlink from synq:** the products stay in Shopify as they are. Synq stops updating their prices and stock.
**Delete N products:** deletes them from Synq and from Shopify for good.

sections.title: What bulk edit doesn't do
list: **Tags:** Synq doesn't add tags.
**Sales channels per product,** archiving and exporting.
**Adding conditions:** add a condition from **Add products**.
**Prices:** set prices with a [price rule](/docs/price-rules) or an [exception](/docs/exceptions).

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Delete can't be undone.** The products are removed from your Shopify store too.
**Unlink keeps the product.** To manage it again, use [Link products you already have](/docs/link-products).

meta.title: Cost and margin · Synq help center
meta.description: Enter what you paid for your cards to see your margin, and to set a minimum so a card never sells under cost.

cost-margin.title: Cost and margin
cost-margin.intro: Enter what you paid for your cards to see your margin, and to set a minimum so a card never sells under cost.

sections.title: What cost is
paragraphs: Cost is Shopify's Cost per item, per condition. Synq and Shopify share it, so an edit in either place shows in both.

sections.title: Set your cost
list: **When you add a card:** **Cost paid** in **Pricing configuration**, as an amount or a percent of market (1 to 100%).
**For many products:** **Inventory** › select products › **Cost** panel.
**A default for new products:** **Settings** › **Pricing** › **What you pay** › **Share of market price**. Leave it empty for no default cost.
**Linked products** bring the cost they have in Shopify.

sections.title: See your margin
paragraphs: Show the **Cost** and **Margin** columns in **Inventory** with **Columns**.
Margin is the **Listed** price minus cost, with its percent. A red **Below cost** badge marks products selling under cost.
Sort by cost or margin to find them fast.

sections.title: Never sell under cost
paragraphs: In a price rule's **Define minimum** step, pick **Your cost** and add a percent or an amount. See [Minimums and rounding](/docs/minimums-rounding).

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Cost doesn't change prices by itself.** Only a minimum based on cost uses it.
**No cost means no cost minimum** for that product.

meta.title: What Synq creates in your store · Synq help center
meta.description: Each card you add becomes a regular Shopify product. Here's what Synq fills in.

what-synq-creates.title: What Synq creates in your store
what-synq-creates.intro: Each card you add becomes a regular Shopify product. Here's what Synq fills in.

sections.title: The product
list: **One product per card and printing,** with one variant per condition under a "Condition" option.
**Title:** the card name by default. See [Product titles and descriptions](/docs/templates).
**Description:** the card's text from TCGplayer.
**Images:** up to 3, from the printing or the card.
**Vendor:** the game's publisher.
**Product type:** the game's name.
**Category:** Gaming Cards for singles and decks, Collectible Trading Cards for sealed.

sections.title: Stock, price and cost
list: **Stock** is tracked at the location you pick.
**Price** comes from the rule or exception that prices the card.
**Cost per item** is filled when you enter a cost.

sections.title: Status, channels and collections
list: **Status:** Draft or Active. Draft is the default, and you can switch it in the add window.
**Channels:** the ones you tick. Synq manages Online Store, Shop and Point of Sale.
**Collection:** the game's singles or sealed collection.

sections.title: SKU and barcode
paragraphs: With Shopify POS installed, each condition gets the TCGplayer SKU and a barcode. See [Sell in your shop with Shopify POS](/docs/pos).

sections.title: Good to know
list: **No tags.** Synq doesn't add tags to products.
**No duplicates.** Synq marks each product with its card and printing, so the same printing can't be created twice.
**Drafts stay hidden.** Publish them in Shopify, or use **Set as active** in **Inventory**.

meta.title: Product titles and descriptions · Synq help center
meta.description: Templates decide how a new product's title, description and search engine text read. Set them per game and per kind of product.

templates.title: Product titles and descriptions
templates.intro: Templates decide how a new product's title, description and search engine text read. Set them per game and per kind of product.

sections.title: Where to find them
paragraphs: Open **Settings** › **Online Store**. Home's **Change how cards read** button opens the same page.
Templates can differ by game and by kind: Singles, Sealed, Decks and Accessories.

sections.title: Title and description
paragraphs: The title is `{name}` by default, the card name only. The description is the card's text.
Add card details to a title from this list:
list: Product name
Set and Set code
Number
Rarity
Printing
Kind
Game and Vendor
Product description

sections.title: Search engine title and description
paragraphs: Search engine text is off by default. Turn it on to fill it for every new product.
You can also set a theme template, so card products use a page layout from your theme.

sections.title: Update products you already have
paragraphs: A template applies to new products. To bring existing products in line, click **Update products** on the same page. It runs in the background.
Products you edited in Shopify keep your edits. Synq tells you how many kept them.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Condition names** (Near Mint or NM) are under **Condition variants** on the same page. See [Conditions and printings](/docs/conditions-printings).
**Title for one card.** Change it in the add window before you click **Add to store**.

meta.title: What stays in sync with Shopify · Synq help center
meta.description: Synq and Shopify share stock, cost and product details. Prices are the one thing your price rules own.

sync.title: What stays in sync with Shopify
sync.intro: Synq and Shopify share stock, cost and product details. Prices are the one thing your price rules own.

head: You change in Shopify
What Synq does
rows: Shows it as Listed. The rule's next run replaces it, unless the condition is excluded
Add, rename or close a location

sections.title: Prices
paragraphs: A price you edit in Shopify admin lasts until the next run of the product's rule.
To keep a price, set it in Synq: edit **Listed** in **Inventory**. That excludes the condition from rules. See [Exceptions](/docs/exceptions).

sections.title: Locations
paragraphs: Stock is kept per location. When you don't pick one, new stock goes to your primary location.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Edits you made stay** when you update products from a template.
**Unlinked products** stay in Shopify, and Synq stops updating them.

meta.title: Sell in your shop with Shopify POS · Synq help center
meta.description: With Shopify POS, every card and condition gets its own barcode, so a scan at the counter rings up the exact card.

pos.title: Sell in your shop with Shopify POS
pos.intro: With Shopify POS, every card and condition gets its own barcode, so a scan at the counter rings up the exact card.

sections.title: Point of Sale settings
paragraphs: Open **Settings** › **Point of Sale**. It needs Shopify POS installed. Without it, the settings are greyed out.
All of these are on at first:
list: **Include new products in Point of Sale:** adds new products to the POS sales channel.
**Sealed products:** the UPC printed on the box, or a Synq code when there isn't one.
**Single cards:** a unique code for each condition.
**TCGplayer SKUs** on each condition.

sections.title: Print labels
steps: Install Shopify's free **Retail Barcode Labels** app.
Print labels for your products. Skip that app's option to create barcodes, since Synq already did.
Stick the label on the card's sleeve or top loader.
paragraphs: Synq doesn't print labels itself.

sections.title: At the counter
paragraphs: A scan rings up the exact card and condition. Stock goes down online too.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Codes are made when a product is created.** Products added before POS was installed may not have them.
**Change a code** for one card in the add window, under **Point of Sale**.
**Home's POS step** shows when Shopify POS is installed: **Set up Shopify POS**.

meta.title: Uninstall Synq · Synq help center
meta.description: Uninstall Synq from your Shopify admin. Your products stay in your store.

uninstall.title: Uninstall Synq
uninstall.intro: Uninstall Synq from your Shopify admin. Your products stay in your store.

sections.title: Uninstall
steps: In your Shopify admin, open **Settings** › **Apps**.
Find Synq and click **Uninstall**.

sections.title: What happens
list: **Your products stay in Shopify** with their prices, stock and details.
**Prices stop updating.** No rule runs after you uninstall.
**About 48 hours later,** Shopify asks Synq to erase your store's data, and Synq does.

sections.title: Install again
paragraphs: Within 48 hours, Synq picks up where you left off.
After that, Synq starts fresh. You go through the setup again, and you may need to link your products again with [Link products you already have](/docs/link-products).

sections.title: Good to know
list: **To stop paying only,** move to the Free plan instead. See [Billing, upgrades and cancelling](/docs/billing).
**Stop one product** without uninstalling: **Inventory** › ⋯ › **Unlink from synq**.

meta.title: Plans and product limits · Synq help center
meta.description: Plans differ only in how many products you can have. Every feature is on every plan, Free included.

plans.title: Plans and product limits
plans.intro: Plans differ only in how many products you can have. Every feature is on every plan, Free included.

sections.title: The plans
paragraphs: Yearly works out to about $19, $53 and $99 a month.

sections.title: What the limit counts
paragraphs: The limit counts products. One product is one card in one printing, with all its conditions and any stock.
Ten Near Mint copies and two Lightly Played copies of one printing are one product.

sections.title: On every plan
list: Every game
Price rules with daily schedules
Spreadsheet and TCGplayer imports
Shopify POS barcodes
Bulk edits in Inventory

sections.title: Near or at your limit
paragraphs: **Inventory** and **Add products** show how many products you use.
On Free, the bar turns amber at 80 products and red at 100.
At the limit, new products can't be added or imported. Products you have keep working: stock, price runs and Shopify sync carry on.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **Moving to a smaller plan deletes nothing.** If you're over its limit, you can't add new products until you're under it.
**Trials.** Paid plans start with a free trial. Shopify's plan page shows its length.

meta.title: Billing, upgrades and cancelling · Synq help center
meta.description: Synq bills through Shopify. Charges show on your Shopify invoice, and you change plans on Shopify's plan page.

billing.title: Billing, upgrades and cancelling
billing.intro: Synq bills through Shopify. Charges show on your Shopify invoice, and you change plans on Shopify's plan page.

sections.title: Upgrade or change plan
steps: Click **Upgrade** in **Inventory** or **Add products**, or **Change plan** in **Settings** › **Billing**.
Shopify's plan page for Synq opens.
Pick a plan, monthly or yearly, and approve it.

sections.title: Invoices
paragraphs: Open **Settings** › **Billing** › **Manage** to see your invoices on Shopify.
Synq charges appear on your Shopify invoice, with your other apps.

sections.title: Downgrade
paragraphs: Pick a smaller plan on Shopify's plan page. Nothing is deleted.
If you have more products than the new limit, you can't add new ones until you're under it.

sections.title: Cancel
paragraphs: Cancel your paid plan from **Change plan** on Shopify's plan page. Your store moves to Free, with up to 100 products.
Your products, rules and stock stay. To stop using Synq completely, see [Uninstall Synq](/docs/uninstall).

sections.title: Good to know
list: **After a free trial,** a store with no paid plan is on Free, with up to 100 products.
**Every feature** is on every plan, so you only pay for more products. See [Plans and product limits](/docs/plans).

meta.title: Get help · Synq help center
meta.description: Write to us from Home or by email. The founder answers, usually the same day.

help.title: Get help
help.intro: Write to us from Home or by email. The founder answers, usually the same day.

sections.title: From the app
steps: Open **Home**.
Click **Feedback** at the top.
Write your message and send it. It goes straight to the founder's inbox.
paragraphs: You can send one message a minute.

sections.title: By email
paragraphs: Write to [help@synq.cards](mailto:help@synq.cards).

sections.title: What to include
list: **Your store's address,** like yourstore.myshopify.com.
**The card or product,** with its set and printing.
**The page in Synq** and what you clicked.
**A screenshot,** if you have one.

sections.title: What's new
paragraphs: Click **What's new** on Home to read what changed in Synq. A number shows how many notes you haven't read.

sections.title: Good to know
list: **A missing game.** Ask with **Feedback**, or with **Request this game** in the spreadsheet import.
**Price questions.** Check the rule's preview and **Activity** first. See [Preview, run and schedule](/docs/run-and-schedule).

meta.title: Terms of Service · Synq
meta.description: The terms that govern your use of Synq, the Shopify trading card pricing and inventory app.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: The short version: your store and your data are yours, you stay in control of your prices, and you can leave whenever you want. The details are below; if anything isn't clear, write to us at iamtelmoo@gmail.com.

sections.title: Who we are
body: Synq ("we", "us") makes a Shopify app for trading card stores ("Synq ‑ TCG Card Manager"). These terms cover the app, this website and any related service (the "Service"). Our legal details are in the [legal notice](/legal), and you can always reach us at iamtelmoo@gmail.com.

sections.title: What Synq does
body: Synq helps you find cards and sealed products in a catalog, add them to your Shopify store, keep their stock in sync and, if you want, keep their prices in step with the market. It only does what the permissions you approve at install allow. If you use Synq for a business, these terms apply to that business.

sections.title: Your store is yours
body: Your products, stock, prices and store data belong to you. We only use them to run Synq for you. If you uninstall, we delete them as described in our [Privacy Policy](/privacy), and the products in your Shopify store stay exactly where they are.
You know your store best, so what it sells and publishes is your call, along with the laws and platform rules that apply to your business.

sections.title: Prices: you stay in control
body: Market prices in Synq come from third parties, mainly TCGplayer. They can be late or wrong, and card markets move fast.

Automatic price updates follow the rules you set: strategy, rounding, minimum prices and which products are included. Because you choose those rules, the prices they produce are yours, and we can't take responsibility for a sale made at one of them, even when the market data behind it was off. A minimum price and a quick look at price changes now and then go a long way; if something looks wrong, tell us and we'll look into it.

sections.title: Card images and trademarks
body: Card images, names and set symbols belong to their publishers, such as The Pokémon Company, Wizards of the Coast and Konami. Synq isn't affiliated with or endorsed by any of them, or by TCGplayer.

The images Synq adds to your products are there so shoppers can see which card they're buying. They come mainly from TCGplayer's public catalog and community card databases. They aren't ours, so we can't license them to you, and how you use them is up to you. You can swap any of them for your own photos whenever you like.

list: Synq has a free plan and paid plans, billed monthly or yearly through Shopify. Charges appear on your Shopify invoice.
You can change or cancel your plan at any time from the app, and uninstalling cancels it too.
Payments already made aren't refunded, except where the law says otherwise. If you think we charged you by mistake, write to us and we'll put it right.
If our prices change, we'll tell you at least 30 days ahead, and the new price starts with your next billing period.

sections.title: Fair use
body: To keep Synq working well for every store, please don't:

list: use it for anything unlawful;
use it or its catalog data to build a competing product or database, or resell access to it;
access it by automated means outside the app, or put unusual load on it;
try to get into systems or data that aren't yours.

sections.title: Keeping Synq running
body: We work hard to keep Synq up and accurate, but it depends on Shopify and other providers, so we can't promise it will never be down or never make a mistake. We keep improving it, which means features can change; if we ever remove one your paid plan relies on, we'll tell you in advance.

sections.title: What belongs to us
body: The Synq software, website, name and design are ours. While you have the app installed, you're free to use them through the Service.

sections.title: The legal part
body: Every software company needs this section. Here is ours, as plainly as we can put it:

list: Synq is provided "as is". As far as the law allows, we don't give warranties beyond what these terms say, including about the accuracy of catalog or price data.

As far as the law allows, we aren't liable for indirect losses such as lost profits, sales or data, and our total liability for any claim is limited to what you paid us in the 12 months before it. Nothing here limits what the law doesn't allow to be limited.
If someone makes a claim against us because of something in your store, such as your listings or your use of images, or because these terms were broken, that claim is yours to handle.

sections.title: If things end
body: You can stop using Synq any time by uninstalling it. We would only suspend an account if these terms are broken or the Service is being harmed, and unless it's urgent we'll talk to you first and give you a chance to sort it out.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
body: If we update these terms, we change the date at the top. For anything that matters, we'll let you know by email or in the app at least 15 days before it applies. Continuing to use Synq after that means you accept the update.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Our rule is simple: collect only what Synq needs to do its job, and never sell it. Here is what that means in practice.

sections.title: Who we are
body: Synq ("we", "us") makes a Shopify app that helps trading card stores list cards, keep stock in sync and price them from market data. This policy covers the app and this website. Our legal details are in the [legal notice](/legal). For anything about your data, write to iamtelmoo@gmail.com.

sections.title: What we collect
body: We collect only what we need to run the app:

list: **Store details**: your shop's domain, name, contact email, currency and timezone, from Shopify when you install.
**Staff details**: the name and email of the people who open the app.
**Catalog data**: the products, variants, inventory, locations and sales channels Synq manages for you.
**Event players**, only if you use Events: the name and player ID each customer enters when they book a seat, the email you add so a player can get store credit, and the order their ticket came from.

**Analytics**: how the app is used (pages opened, clicks, browser and device), so we can see where it gets in your way. This covers Synq's pages only, never the rest of your Shopify admin or your screen.
**Messages**: what you send us by email, the contact form or Shopify's support channel.

body: Apart from Events, Synq doesn't collect your customers' data. Passwords and payment details never pass through it.

sections.title: How we use it

list: To run the app: create and update your products, sync stock and prices, run imports and bill your plan.
To run Events for you: seat players from their orders, check them in, refund them when you take them off, and give them store credit and prizes.
To help you when you write to us, and to send service emails such as job results or billing notices.
To find and fix problems and decide what to build next.
To keep the service secure and prevent abuse.
To keep the billing and tax records the law requires.

body: We never sell your data or use it for advertising. Your customers' data is used only to run your events: never for marketing, and never to train AI models.
If you are in the EU or UK: we rely on our contract with you to run the app, on our legitimate interest to improve and secure it, and on legal obligation for billing records.

sections.title: Who we share it with
body: Only with the providers that run parts of Synq for us, under contracts that limit them to our instructions: Render (app hosting), Supabase (database), Trigger.dev (background jobs), Cloudflare (image storage), Resend (email), PostHog (app analytics) and Google (website analytics, only if you accept cookies). On the pages that show your customers, analytics records no text, so their names and contacts never reach PostHog.
We may also disclose data when the law requires it, or to a buyer if Synq is ever sold, under this same policy.

sections.title: Shopify and merchants
body: Synq works through the permissions you approve when you install it: products, inventory, locations and sales channels. If you use Events, Synq also asks for your orders and customers, and gives those permissions back if you stop. For the data in your store, Synq acts on your behalf.

Shopify sends us its privacy requests and we answer them. When you uninstall, Shopify asks us to erase your store's data 48 hours later and we delete it. The products in your store stay there; they are yours.

**Our data processing terms.** For your customers' data you are the controller and Synq is your processor. We process it only to run Events, on your instructions and under this policy; keep it confidential; use only the providers listed above; help you answer your customers' requests; tell you without undue delay about a breach that affects it; and delete it as described below. This section is our data processing agreement with you. Write to us for a signed copy.

If you shop at a store that uses Synq, your data is held by that store and Shopify. When you book one of its events, the store uses Synq to keep your name, player ID and the order your ticket came from, on its behalf. Please contact the store about it.

list: Store, staff and catalog data: while the app is installed, then deleted after uninstall as above.
Event players: names, player IDs and contacts are removed 180 days after the event. The seat record stays, without them. Everything goes 48 hours after you uninstall.
Analytics: for the retention period of our analytics plan, then deleted.
Messages: as long as needed to help you.
Billing records: as long as tax law requires.

sections.title: Security
body: Data is encrypted in transit and at rest, backups included. Access to production systems is limited to the people who run Synq, and every read and write is scoped to a single store. No system is perfectly secure; if a breach affects your data or your customers', we will tell you and the authorities as the law requires.

sections.title: International transfers
body: Several of our providers are in the United States. Those transfers rely on the EU–US Data Privacy Framework where the provider is certified, and otherwise on the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses.

sections.title: Cookies
body: The app keeps a small analytics identifier in your browser's local storage, and Shopify uses its own cookies to sign you in. This website uses Google Analytics cookies only if you accept them in the cookie banner, and no advertising cookies.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You can ask us to access, correct, delete or export your personal data, or object to how we use it. Write to iamtelmoo@gmail.com and we will answer within a month.
In the EU you can also complain to your data protection authority; ours is Spain's Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (aepd.es).

sections.title: Changes to this policy
body: When we change this policy we update the date at the top. If a change matters, we tell you by email or in the app first.

cookies.title: Cookies Policy
cookies.intro: This Cookies Policy explains what cookies are, which cookies we use on synq.cards (the "Site") and inside the Synq application, and how you can control them.

sections.title: 1. What are cookies
body: Cookies are small text files stored on your device when you visit a website. They allow the site to remember your actions and preferences over time. Similar technologies such as localStorage, sessionStorage and pixels are covered by this policy.

sections.title: 2. Cookies we use
body: Strictly necessary cookies: required for the Site and application to function (session, authentication, security, language preference). These cookies do not require your consent under Spanish law.
Your cookie choice: we keep your answer to the cookie banner in your browser's local storage (synq-consent) so we don't ask again. This is strictly necessary and needs no consent.

Analytics without cookies: we use Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights to count visits and measure page speed. They set no cookies and do not track you across sites. When you arrive, we also keep in session storage, for that visit only, the page and link that brought you here, so a message you send through the contact form can say how you found us. Nothing is kept if your browser sends Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track.

Analytics cookies (only with your consent): if you accept them, we load Google Analytics 4 (Google Ireland Limited) to see how visitors find and use the Site, which pages they open and whether they go on to the Shopify App Store listing. It sets the cookies _ga (2 years) and _ga_<ID> (2 years). Google Signals and advertising features are off, and Google does not keep full IP addresses. Google may process the data in the United States under the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. If you reject them, or your browser sends Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track, Google Analytics never loads.
We do not use advertising cookies.

sections.title: 3. How to manage cookies
body: You can accept or reject analytics cookies at any time from "Cookie settings" in the footer of every page. Rejecting them after accepting stops Google Analytics and deletes its cookies.
You can also configure your browser to refuse cookies, delete existing ones or alert you when cookies are being set. Most browsers offer this option under "Settings" or "Preferences".
If you disable strictly necessary cookies, some features of the Site or the application may not work properly.

sections.title: 4. Changes to this policy
body: We may update this Cookies Policy. Material changes will be communicated via the Site.

sections.title: 5. Contact
body: Questions about this policy can be sent to help@synq.cards.
